newsitem.title: POLAND: BIG says Gdanski buy to cut its '97 profit.
newsitem.headline: BIG says Gdanski buy to cut its '97 profit.

text.p: Polish Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG), whose 1996 profits were cut by a 31.2- percent purchase of Bank Gdanski, expects 1997 to be tough too as it tries to up its stake, BIG's president said.
"1997 will be a tough year because our (financial) obligations are likely to be unprecedented," Boguslaw Kott told a news conference on Thursday.

Kott said BIG's net profit of 55.2 million zlotys for its 1995/96 financial year was cut by 24 to 25 million zlotys due to its purchase of Gdanski in late 1995. BIG increased its stake in Gdanski to 31.23 percent in September 1996.
Kott declined to forecast BIG's 1997 earnings.
The bank was the only bidder for the treasury's December 1996 offer of 31.9 percent, or 6,260,240 shares, of Gdanski.

Kott would not say how the bank would fund its prospective stake increase in Gdanski, but said a share or bond issue was possible. He said BIG might offer to buy the rest of Gdanski shares if shareholders wanted.
He said the Gdanski buy might prevent BIG from paying out a 1996 dividend, but that a decision would be made by late March.
"It's hard to share out profit when you have such investment," he said.

Kott told Reuters he could not rule out the bank's participation in future privatisations of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) or Bank Zachodni SA or in a potential share issue by the life insurer PZU Zycie SA, but that BIG was currently concentrating on Gdanski.
Kott said BIG's 1996 results were also hurt by a capital raise for the wholly-owned subsidiary BIG Bank SA. BIG's group net rose to 110 million zlotys from 75 million the year before.
Kott noted that group return on equity, which inched up to 31.9 percent from 31.8 percent, did better compared to inflation, which shrank September-to-September to 19.5 percent from 24.4 percent.
